headline: Brazilian Real Plummets Against U.S. Dollar Following Stronger-Than-Expected US Payrolls
summary: The U.S. dollar closed above R$ 5.50 on Friday, reaching its highest closing level since late 2025 following U.S. payroll data that exceeded economists' expectations.
why: Stronger US employment data influences Federal Reserve rate expectations, driving capital flows out of emerging markets and weakening currencies like the Brazilian real.

impacts.name: US Dollar / Brazilian Real
impacts.why: Stronger US jobs data boosts the dollar against emerging market currencies.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected US payroll data led to expectations of higher US interest rates, strengthening the dollar and pushing the exchange rate above R$ 5.50.
